skills.name: Apartment hunt onboarding
skills.description: Use this on first wake after install, or when the user wants to set or reset apartment-hunt criteria, preferences, commute limits, and anti-jobs.
skills.content:
---
name: Apartment hunt onboarding
description: >-
  Use this on first wake after install, or when the user wants to set or reset
  apartment-hunt criteria, preferences, commute limits, and anti-jobs.
---
# Apartment hunt onboarding

Run this on the first message after install, or whenever the user says they want to restart criteria.

## Goal
Lock hard filters and soft preferences into agent memory, create or resume the daily listing routine, and stay quiet until the next search is useful. Do not invent cities, budgets, move-in dates, or commute targets.

## Ask once (batch with a widget when helpful)
Collect only what you need to search. Skip anything already in memory.

1. **Where** — city/neighborhoods, and must-be-near landmarks (transit stop, office, school).
2. **Commute** — one or more destinations (work, school, partner's office) with a hard max door-to-door time in minutes, preferred modes (walk, transit, bike, drive), and whether peak rush hour matters. Optional soft target (e.g. prefer under 30, hard cap 45). If they only care about walk-to-transit, capture that as a landmark walk minutes instead.
3. **Beds / baths** — hard numbers (e.g. 2 bed AND 2 bath). Note if 1 bed + den is acceptable.
4. **Hard rent cap** — monthly max they will not stretch past.
5. **Move-in window** — earliest and latest; whether later dates are OK if clearly better.
6. **Must-haves** — in-unit laundry, parking, pets, outdoor space, elevator, etc.
7. **Deal-breakers** — broker fee, ground floor, no AC, long walk to transit, commute over the hard max, etc.
8. **Search sources** — default Zillow, StreetEasy (or local equivalent), apartments.com, plus official building sites. Ask if they want others.
9. **Delivery** — preferred digest time in their timezone (default 9:00 local), and whether quiet empty runs are OK (default yes: no message if the shortlist is unchanged).
10. **Anti-jobs** — confirm they book tours themselves; this bot never emails, texts, applies, or contacts brokers/landlords unless they later unlock that with a different bot (Inbox/CoS pattern).
11. **Coordinator** — optional: name of another bot or person to flag only for send/hold mail, drop-a-building, or hours-left deadlines. Default: no fan-out; recs stay in this chat.

## Save
Write profile-tier memories for:
- Hard filters (location, commute destinations + max minutes + modes, beds/baths, cap, move-in, must-haves, deal-breakers)
- Soft preferences and scoring weights (including preferred commute soft target)
- Anti-jobs and who owns email/applications
- Digest time + quiet-empty-runs rule
- Optional coordinator escalation rules

Keep live shortlists and promo state in log memory, never frozen inside the daily routine prompt.

## Standing routine
Create or update a daily (or weekday) listing-recs routine whose prompt says: load hard filters from memory, search the agreed sources, estimate commute against saved destinations, surface 3–6 best with tour links only when something changed, stay quiet on empty runs, delete itself when they sign a lease. Schedule in their local timezone at the agreed hour.

## First search
Offer one immediate scan after onboarding. If they decline, wait for the first scheduled run.

## Pause modes
If they apply somewhere primary: pause tour pushes, track that application, surface only status changes or hours-left deadlines, and stay dormant until they or their coordinator wakes you. If they sign a lease: delete the daily routine and offer a short move-in checklist once.

skills.name: Daily listing scan
skills.description: Use this when running a scheduled or on-demand apartment listing search against the user's saved hard filters, including commute-time limits.
skills.content:
---
name: Daily listing scan
description: >-
  Use this when running a scheduled or on-demand apartment listing search
  against the user's saved hard filters, including commute-time limits.
---
# Daily listing scan

## Load
Read hard filters (including commute destinations, max minutes, and modes), soft preferences, anti-jobs, and the last shortlist from memory. If onboarding is incomplete, stop and run Apartment hunt onboarding instead.

## Search
Check the agreed listing sites (default Zillow, StreetEasy / local MLS aggregator, apartments.com) plus official building pages when a listing is thin or captcha-walled. Confirm real unit rent, beds/baths, and move-in date — never a marketing "from $" alone.

## Commute filter
For each candidate that otherwise fits, estimate door-to-door time to every saved destination using the preferred modes (walk, transit, bike, drive). Prefer live maps/transit directions when available; otherwise be explicit that the estimate is approximate.
- Drop listings over the hard commute max for any required destination.
- Prefer those under the soft target when ranking.
- On surfaced recs, show estimated minutes + mode to each destination (e.g. "28 min transit to Midtown, 12 min walk to PATH").
- If commute cannot be estimated, say so and do not pretend a listing passes a hard commute filter.

## Filter
Drop anything over the hard rent cap, wrong bed/bath, outside the area, over the hard commute max, or outside the move-in window unless memory says a stretch is allowed. Flag deal-breakers.

## Diff
Compare to the last shortlist. Material = appeared, dropped, price/availability/commute change, or a promo/apply-by deadline that blows in hours.

## Quiet empty runs
If nothing material changed, send no message. No recap. No "(no change.)".

## When you surface
Send 3–6 best in chat with: building/unit, rent, beds/baths, size if known, commute estimates, transit/landmark, move-in, URL. Lead with what changed. Add all-in notes when visible (fees, parking, utilities, concessions).

## Never
Do not email, text, apply, or contact brokers/landlords. Do not book tours. Do not spam a coordinator with the same list — flag them only for send/hold mail, drop-a-building, or hours-left deadlines.

## After
Update log memory with today's shortlist and any promo/deadline state. If they signed a lease, delete the daily routine.

skills.name: Application and deal tracker
skills.description: Use this when the user applies somewhere, gets an approval/condition, or needs a pause while an application is primary.
skills.content:
---
name: Application and deal tracker
description: >-
  Use this when the user applies somewhere, gets an approval/condition, or needs
  a pause while an application is primary.
---
# Application and deal tracker

## When they apply
1. Save the building/unit, rent, co-applicants, portal, and open tasks (income verify, pet screening, deposit) in profile memory as PRIMARY.
2. Pause tour pushes: keep quiet scans if useful, but do not suggest new tours unless they ask.
3. Flag their coordinator only if the unit disappears or status clearly changes.
4. Offer to pause the daily listing routine entirely until they wake you.

## Status updates
Track Approve / Deny / Approve-with-conditions / docs still open. Surface conditions plainly (e.g. extra deposit for rental history) without nagging.

## Deal / deadline radar
Watch apply-by promos, free months, and deposit specials on buildings they care about. Surface only when the deadline is hours away or they asked for backups. Never apply for them.

## Resume or end
- Rejected or they reopen the hunt: resume daily recs and clear PRIMARY.
- Signed a lease: delete the daily routine, clear the hunt, offer a one-time move-in checklist (utilities, renter's insurance, movers, parking, keys).

skills.name: Tour prep brief
skills.description: Use this when the user books or asks about a tour and wants questions, commute notes, red flags, and all-in cost for a specific listing.
skills.content:
---
name: Tour prep brief
description: >-
  Use this when the user books or asks about a tour and wants questions, commute
  notes, red flags, and all-in cost for a specific listing.
---
# Tour prep brief

For one listing (or a short same-day slate), send a compact brief:

1. **Fit** — how it matches hard filters and soft preferences, including commute vs hard max and soft target.
2. **Commute** — estimated door-to-door minutes and mode to each saved destination; note peak vs off-peak if that mattered in onboarding; flag if the estimate could not be verified.
3. **All-in cost** — rent + known fees, parking, utilities, concessions; monthly and move-in cash if estimable.
4. **Ask on site** — lease length, concession fine print, package/mail, laundry, noise, HVAC, pest history, broker fee, application timeline.
5. **Red flags** — bait pricing, 1bed+den sold as 2/2, stale third-party pages vs official inventory, long walk vs claimed transit, commute over the hard max.
6. **Compare** — one line vs the current shortlist leaders on rent, size, and commute.

Do not contact the building. Do not email or apply. Keep it short enough to read on the way over.
